rules.label: Decisions made right now
rules.example: The phone is ringing. I'll answer it!

rules.label: Guesses and opinions
rules.example: I think it will be fun.

rules.label: Plans made before now
rules.example: I bought tickets. I'm going to watch a film.

rules.label: Things you can see happening
rules.example: Look at those black clouds! It's going to rain.

warmup.context_clue: You just noticed there is no milk in the fridge.
warmup.sentence_prompt: Oh, we are out of milk! I ___ go to the shop right now.
warmup.disambiguation_note: You just found out now, so this is a sudden decision.

warmup.context_clue: You wrote 'buy milk' on your shopping list this morning.
warmup.sentence_prompt: I have my shopping list ready. I ___ buy some milk after school.
warmup.disambiguation_note: You planned this earlier today, before speaking.

warmup.context_clue: You are talking about weather next summer.
warmup.sentence_prompt: I think next July ___ be very hot.
warmup.disambiguation_note: 'I think' introduces a personal guess, not physical proof.

warmup.context_clue: You are looking at a weather map showing 45°C tomorrow.
warmup.sentence_prompt: Look at the temperature on the screen! Tomorrow ___ be very hot.
warmup.disambiguation_note: You can see the evidence on the screen right now.

warmup.context_clue: Your friend drops their pencils on the floor.
warmup.sentence_prompt: Don't worry, I ___ pick them up for you.
warmup.disambiguation_note: You are offering to help immediately.

warmup.context_clue: Your friend asks why you are holding a broom.
warmup.sentence_prompt: I ___ clean the classroom floor before the bell rings.
warmup.disambiguation_note: Holding the broom shows that you already planned to clean.

questions.context_clue: The classroom is really hot and stuffy.
questions.sentence_prompt: I ___ open the window to get some fresh air.
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'will' for decisions made at the exact moment of speaking.

questions.context_clue: Sara already bought her train ticket yesterday.
questions.sentence_prompt: Sara ___ visit her grandparents this weekend.
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'be going to' for plans decided before the moment of speaking.

questions.context_clue: Look at those huge, black clouds in the sky!
questions.sentence_prompt: Take an umbrella! It ___ rain very soon.
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'be going to' when you can see clear evidence right now.

questions.context_clue: Your friend is carrying a heavy stack of books.
questions.sentence_prompt: Here, let me help. I ___ carry some of those for you.
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'will' when offering to help someone right away.

questions.context_clue: Tom saved all his pocket money for three months.
questions.sentence_prompt: Tom ___ buy a new skateboard on Saturday.
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'be going to' when someone already has an intention or plan.

questions.context_clue: You are guessing about a football match next year.
questions.sentence_prompt: I think our school team ___ win the championship!
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'will' with 'I think' to give a personal opinion or guess.

questions.context_clue: We checked the cinema website and the film is sold out.
questions.sentence_prompt: We ___ watch the movie tonight after all.
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'aren't going to' when a previously made plan changes or is cancelled.

questions.context_clue: Your little brother wants to read your private diary.
questions.sentence_prompt: No! You ___ read my diary—it's a secret!
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'won't' for a strong refusal or a promise not to do something.

questions.context_clue: Ali is running too fast on the wet floor.
questions.sentence_prompt: Watch out! He ___ slip and fall!
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'be going to' because you can see the danger happening right now.

questions.context_clue: You want to ask a classmate about their weekend plans.
questions.sentence_prompt: What ___ do after school on Friday?
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'Are you going to...?' to ask about someone's existing plans.

questions.context_clue: You need help with a difficult maths problem.
questions.sentence_prompt: ___ you help me with question number five, please?
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'Will you...?' when asking someone for a favour or help right now.

questions.context_clue: The waiter asks what you want to drink at a cafe.
questions.sentence_prompt: Hmm, I ___ have a glass of orange juice, please.
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'will' when ordering food or making a quick choice.

questions.context_clue: The students packed their bags and are wearing sports clothes.
questions.sentence_prompt: Class 7B ___ play basketball in the gym next.
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'be going to' because the preparation shows the plan is already set. 'Class 7B' is treated as one group.

questions.context_clue: You forgot to bring your homework to school today.
questions.sentence_prompt: I promise I ___ bring it to your desk tomorrow morning.
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'will' after 'I promise' to guarantee an action.

questions.context_clue: Your friend didn't study at all for the science test.
questions.sentence_prompt: She didn't revise, so she ___ pass the exam easily.
questions.feedback_tip: Use 'isn't going to' when the present facts point to a likely result.
